utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, can we go into closed session? There's just a matter I need to address you regarding the witnesses, and it concerns confidential details of one particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this unit, sir, that protected the village, did it have any type of patrol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us: What did this patrol do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They patrolled the village during the night. They guarded the village during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people -- first, how many patrols were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually three patrols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many men were in each of these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two men respectively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what type of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they use any radios to communicate with each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the members of the patrol wear uniforms or civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these patrols located in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was located at the entrance into the village, the other one at the exit out of the village, and the third one in the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any roadblocks that were established by these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the patrols do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They monitored who entered the village during the night and who went out of the village during the night, and everything that went on in the village, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there ever involved in any incidents or shootings, these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were the patrols functional?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until Samac fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're talking from January to April 17th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you drafted into these patrols or it was a volunteer -- a voluntary task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was anyone paid for being on these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about some individuals from Bosanski Samac. Do you know a man by the name of Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw him often in my village too. I know that he was a lively man. He liked folk music. I saw him in Samac as well. He was a businessman. Things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know another defendant by the name of Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know he was born in Kruskovo Polje. That is a village next to my village. When we were young, we would sometimes sit at the same table. I know that we had coffee together a few times. He finished medical school. He became a doctor. Things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Miroslav Tadic, another defendant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell the Chamber how you know him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he worked in Bosanski Samac, in the catering business. He had a cafe called Cafe AS. He was fond of gamble, or rather, I should put it this way: I know that there was gambling going on in that cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known each of these people? You indicated you have known Blagoje Simic since you were very young. What about the other two? How long had you known them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Simo Zaric until the war, for about 15 years, and also Miro Brko for about 15 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you to look around the courtroom. Let's start off with Simo Zaric. Is Simo Zaric in the courtroom at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please describe the way he's dressed and tell us Where he's located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Zaric is on my right-hand side. He's wearing a black suit, white shirt, and it seems to me that the tie he is wearing is black as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Miroslav Tadic? You said you know Miroslav Tadic, nicknamed Brko. Could you tell us where he's sitting in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is sitting between Simo Zaric and Blagoje Simic. He's sitting in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on that answer, for the record, could the record indicate that all three defendants have been identified by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's go back to March and April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. I don't think you asked the witness where Dr. Blagoje Simic was sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I didn't because in his last answer he said that Miroslav Tadic was sitting between Simo Zaric and Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Fine. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let's go back to March and April of 1992. Did you travel throughout the municipality of Bosanski Samac during that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were travelling, did you observe any Yugoslavian troops or JNA troops in the villages in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Chamber in what villages you observed troops? Just start off with troops.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village of Obudovac, the village of Batkusa, the village of Donja Slatina, Crkvina, Kruskovo Polje, Milosevac, Skarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it unusual to see JNA troops in those small villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen troops in those villages before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your travels in March and April of 1992, did you see any tanks in those villages? And just tell the Court which ones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Obudovac, the village of Batkusa, Crkvina, Kruskovo Polje, Milosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any mortars which were placed in any villages during that same period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you see the mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them in the village of Skarici, on the road between Samac, Modrica, Gradacac. Actually, near a restaurant called Trile's cafe, in a small thicket. And I also saw mortars in Milosevac. But I would like to point out that Milosevac as a village does not belong to the municipality of Bosanski Samac but to the municipality of Modrica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it unusual to see tanks and mortars in these small villages in the vicinity of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen tanks and mortars in those places previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the witness be shown Exhibit P9D - it's a map - so he can just show the locations of the different areas that he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to -- can you take a look at that, please? Start off -- could you point out where Bosanski Samac is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac is located by the Sava River, right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some of these villages that you mentioned, Kruskovo Polje, Batkusa, Obudovac, could you show us where those are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I'm pointing at now is the road that goes from Samac to Crkvina, and from Crkvina it forks off. This road leads to Modrica, and the road I'm showing now leads to Gradacac. Skarici is here, and the mortars that I saw were out of Samac, by the first and second intersection. The mortars were somewhere around here. In Milosevac, in Milosevac, is where I saw them. But it's not on this map. It would be around here, if the map were full, complete. Crkvina is here, or rather, where the road forks off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us again with Milosevac is, even though it's not on the map? Just show us the area where it would be. If they could adjust the focus, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Milosevac is between the road that leads to Modrica and the road that leads to Gradacac. It takes up part of Lugovi. I can't be more specific. I don't know how the road would continue along here, but at any rate, it goes beyond this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you show us the area where the tanks were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would also be around here. The tanks were located on the road between Modrica and Samac, at a farm that was called Dr. Mujbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, sir. Now, sir, you mentioned that you've known Blagoje Simic for a number of years. In March and April of 1992, just prior to the war, had you ever heard him speaking on the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Court about the speech that you heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion I heard a speech. I cannot say whether he was speaking live or whether it had been recorded, whether it was some previous speech of his. However, what matters is that in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, there has to be Serb authority only, if I can put it that way, and the Croats of Bosanski Samac should move out on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his position, if you know, in the SDS at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was leader of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he make any comments with regard to the HDZ party, the Croatian party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any statements that he had made at any public meetings at that same time, in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall a statement at any public meeting where they talked about who would be controlling the region?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's leading -- a perfectly leading question, and finally, this witness said that he was not aware about any of the speech of Blagoje Simic. I don't know why the Prosecution is pursuing this line of questioning, because he got very clear answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's nothing wrong with the question. Mr. Weiner can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall any statement that Blagoje Simic made -- or were you aware of any statement that he made at a public meeting in relation to who should be controlling the region of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said. I've already referred to his statement in which he said that control should be exercised by the Serbs, that is, the SDS, and that the Croats should move out on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to this, at this same time, you've now seen tanks, you've heard statements from the defendant Blagoje Simic. Were there any rumours spreading throughout Bosanski Samac in the villages in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Is that directed to the facts, personal knowledge of this witness, or to the rumours? I mean, what we are trying here, rumours or facts?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just trying to introduce him into the rumours of war, and then the fright or the panic which was occurring at that time. And he can be aware -- obviously, he can be aware of certain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think you can phrase your question better than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of any rumours relating to war at that time, in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the rumours was this statement of Dr. Blagoje Simic. If one gives it a wider interpretation. And, of course, that's the way people interpreted it and in fact were therefore panic-stricken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were people leaving the villages as a result?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any members of your family leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My wife and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you bring them out of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you leave the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, simply I had no reason to leave my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why didn't you leave your home? Did you want to leave Bosanski Samac, the municipality, at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any intention in the early part of April of leaving the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to April 17th. What did you hear on April 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, I heard that Samac fell into Serb hands, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had you heard was then the mayor, or was now the mayor of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have a radio in your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever listen to the radio at that time, after the takeover of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what station did you listen to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I listened to a station that was called the Serb radio station of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had it always been the Serb radio station of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the fall of Samac, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it called prior to April 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was called Radio Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you hear any of the defendants speaking over that radio station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Blagoje Simic speaking on the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Except on that occasion that I already mentioned, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any restrictions that were placed on non-Serbs after the takeover of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the trial court about some of those restrictions that were placed on non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the crucial limitations was the order by Mr. Stevan Todorovic for persons of non-Serb ethnicity, that they were not allowed to -- not more than two of non-Serb people by ethnicity were not allowed to gather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you saw -- you said the order was issued by Stevan Todorovic. Was there a written poster or a flyer that was distributed with this information, that no more than two non-Serbs could gather or meet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other restrictions or rules were placed on non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about any other restrictions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about vehicles. Were there certain restrictions or was there a certain change, a change placed on vehicles in the villages, those that were owned by non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber what you had to do to your vehicle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In order to move around in my vehicle, I had to visibly place a white band on my car, a white ribbon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Persons of what ethnic group had to place white ribbons on their vehicles in order to move throughout the villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People of Croat or Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you owned a vehicle. Did you have a white ribbon on your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was moving around, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any white ribbons on any of the vehicles owned by Serbs in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of anyone having to wear white armbands at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If a person was going about without their car, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you first learn about the white armbands as well as the ribbons, the white ribbons on the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an order that came to the village that if people were going to use their cars, then they had to place these white markings on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the order came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably from Mr. Stevan Todorovic. In the flyer that I saw, in the pamphlet, there was his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that flyer that you saw, was that the one relating to the not more than two non-Serbs were allowed to meet? Is that the flyer that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were people allowed to leave the municipality at will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the fall of Samac, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What prevented you from leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were prevented by checkpoints in the municipality of Bosanski Samac. In order to leave or pass through any of those checkpoints, I had to have a permit which I was supposed to request from the current Serbian authorities that were acting at the time in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you have to go in Bosanski Samac to get one of these authorisations to leave the municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You had to go -- I didn't go, but people who went, went to the Utva company, and this is where they received those permits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of any of the people who issued those permits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go down and request permission to leave your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't because I wasn't thinking of leaving my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the end of April. Was there a notice in relation to turning in weapons at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Tribunal, or the Trial Chamber, about that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an order which allegedly came from Kruskovo Polje, because that's where a certain number of soldiers were situated, at the local community hall in Kruskovo Polje. So the order came for all the weapons from Hasici to be collected and brought to the entrance of the village of Kruskovo Polje, and that was on the road between Samac and Gradacac. That's where the entrance to the Kruskovo Polje village was. All the weapons were collected. We didn't have any other weapons, other than guns. This is what I'm thinking of: Hunting rifles. So all of these rifles were collected, they were brought here to this point, and then two soldiers came and took all of those rifles to the local commune in Kruskovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you turn your weapon, your hunting rifle, over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were you doing during this period? You had the takeover of Bosanski Samac through the end of the month. What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was growing vegetables and I was also cultivating this field that I mentioned, where I planted the trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that what you continued to do after you turned your weapon in over the next two to four days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did something happen on May 2nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what happened? What were you doing, first? What were you doing around lunch-time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just had lunch and I sat down in the shade in my yard, and I made coffee for myself, which I was planning to drink. So I was just sitting there and I didn't know anything, and then a couple of people came and they arrested me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there others that were arrested after you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they going house to house and arresting everyone, or was there some sort of list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had a list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were arrested in this first group of arrests, or in your group of arrests?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eight people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these civilians or military personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were all civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what ethnic group were these persons who were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were involved in arresting these eight Croatians or Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was arrested, there were four men, but in the process of the arresting, then more people came, so that altogether there were about ten people that will were arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Out of these ten people who were making the arrests, they were out there working together, were these police officers, or were there any police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these soldiers from that were making the arrests?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A number of them were from the municipality of Bosanski Samac, while the rest were people that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later find out where these people were from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they were from Serbia. I concluded that based on the way they spoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it about the way they spoke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had a specific accent which told me that they were from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Once they arrested this group of people, where did they bring you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took me to the headquarters of the Territorial Defence in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that located right across the street from the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got there, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived, they started beating us, right away, the minute we got there, as people were coming out of the truck, they were beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you got off the truck, you and these seven others, and you were beaten immediately. Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same people who arrested us also beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you were beaten, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to a small room in the headquarters of the Territorial Defence. That's where they took us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But prior to that, prior to going to that small room where you were held, later held, did you go into the courtyard of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's where we came out of the truck, into the courtyard of the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have to line up first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, to move things along, I'd like to read some paragraphs to him and ask him if these are accurate, these statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraphs 29 through 34 of the new statement. Sir, what I'm going to do is read to you from the Prosecutor's notes that were taken from you recently and ask you if this information is accurate, rather than spending about an hour testifying, we can do this very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, before you do that, just for the sake of clarity, you say, first of all, here, you're going to read paragraphs 29 and 34 of the new statement, but then you mention the Prosecutor's notes. So can we make sure whether it's the statement that was taken for 92 bis reasons, and if so, have the date and/or the date that the Prosecutor's notes were taken, if we're talking about something different. Just so that we all understand what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was the -- these were -- these -- this really isn't a statement. This was taken for purposes of 92 bis. However, when -- between the time that this statement was taken and the arrival of the witness, the policy changed. As a result, the witness hasn't reviewed this in 92 bis fashion, hasn't signed it. However, yesterday we went over these notes, as we spoke in the proofing session yesterday. So what I was going to do is read those to him, see if he does agree, and if those are in fact the facts. Otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But you are reading this statement as the evidence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If he adopts it, it becomes the evidence of the witness, if he makes changes, that plus it's changes are the evidence. If he doesn't adopt it, then none of it becomes evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "We arrived at the Territorial Defence building at Bosanski Samac, at about 3.00 or 3.30 p.m. Boban Radulovic and the other soldiers and policemen beat me and the other men in my group as we came off the truck. I do not remember who specifically beat me." Sir, is that an accurate portrayal of what happened to you when you got off the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "We were then put in a line against the wall, in the enclosed courtyard of the Territorial Defence building. One by one we were called forward and asked provocative questions. They asked me how many Serbs I killed, how many Serbian women I raped, and how many children I killed with a knife. I did not have any time to answer the questions. I was immediately hit and fell to the ground. They hit me with their fists, police batons, and metal pipes, on my face, fingers, kidney area, legs, and feet. Four additional soldiers joined the beatings. Three of these soldiers went by the nicknames of Lugar, Laki, and Pukovnik. I believe the fourth man went by the name of Crni. I learned these nicknames when they would address each other. I was beaten by Laki, Crni, and the others, who I do not know." Sir, so far what I read, is that an accurate portrayal of happened to you at the Territorial Defence building on May 2nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll continue: "We were beaten until about 5.00 to 5.30 p.m. I was one of the first men who was beaten. I lost consciousness and did not see who beat the other men. I believe I regained consciousness relatively quickly. The soldiers and policemen were hosing us down to revive us. I saw other men lying unconscious next to me. They were also being hosed down with the water. We were not the only ones to be brought in that day. There were other non-Serb males who were brought in on military trucks that day. We were about 20 persons." Sir, what I just read to you, is that an accurate portrayal of what had happened to you on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's continue: "We were taken as a group and placed in one room inside the building. Inside this room, there were already over 40 other men. They were all non-Serb men. Muslims and Croats from Bosanski Samac itself and neighbouring villages. I had difficulty walking, as my feet had swelled after the beating. I noticed my hands were swollen and black and blue. My fingernails were also black and blue. These fingernails eventually fell off later, as the nails healed. I was bruised all over my body. My nose and lip were bleeding. My right eye was swollen shut. The other eight men who were brought to the Territorial Defence building with me also were wounded from this beating. Some of them were in worse shape than me." Sir, is that an accurate portrayal of what happened to you on May 2nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's continue. " We had just enough time to find a place to sit, when Laki, Lugar, Pukovnik, and others, and those others whom I do not know, started taking out most of the men who were in this room. These guards would point out individuals or groups of two or three men. The guards left the door open and I could see out into the courtyard. I saw the men being beaten. I was called out and beaten in the courtyard. I saw that some of the men were already unconscious. Those men who were conscious following the beating returned to the room. Those who were unconscious remained outside until they regained consciousness. When they came to, they had to return to the room." Is that an accurate portrayal of what happened on that date in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I saw Boban Radulovic beat Zlatko Karalic. I was beaten by Laki, Crni, and some other soldiers whom I did not know. Laki, Crni, Pukovnik, and Lugar introduced themselves to us as members of Seselj's group, the White Eagles. After I was beaten, I returned to the room. The soldiers continued to come back into the room the entire night. The people who were not beaten had to sing Chetnik songs. There were no toilet facilities. We received no water or food. During my detention at the Territorial Defence camp, I do not believe anyone from my room was killed." Sir, is that an accurate portrayal of what occurred on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we breaking at 11.00 or 11.30 today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, how long were you held in the TO at that initial visit to the facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Less than two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the next day. Where were you brought on the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken across the street to the building of the then police station in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Time to break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break until 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. The Prosecution is proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when we left off, you were being held the first day at the TO, and then that second day they brought you across the street to the police station. Sometime when you were at the TO, in the police station, on that second day, did they bring you anywhere to get you any food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever brought anywhere while you were being held in Bosanski Samac for food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you brought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The restaurant of the Sit work organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were brought to the -- what you call the cafeteria or restaurant at that company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were there, did you see any of the defendants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Simo Zaric doing -- or first, where was he when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was standing with some colleagues of his, and his back was turned to me and to the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where were you taken after you were fed at the Sit company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, they returned us to the Territorial Defence headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time had you spent at the SUP, or the police building, that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I stayed there for perhaps three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read this statement, paragraph 41, and why don't you tell me if this is an accurate depiction of what happened at the police station on the morning of May 3rd: "The next morning, 3rd of May, possibly around 9.00 a.m., six or seven of us were brought over to the prison in the police building. One of those in the cells was Luka Gregurovic, who had been with the police. He was so badly beaten, he could hardly talk. I stayed in the prison for about three days. During this time I heard screaming all the time, coming from other parts of the building. I was beaten every day except one. On each of these days, I was beaten two or three times, sometimes even more. One of the soldiers I saw there was Slobodan Vakic, nicknamed Zvaka. Two or three other soldiers would also beat me, but I do not know their names. The people who would come in and beat us were Serb paramilitaries with Serb accents. They would use police batons or implements, like table legs and so on, to beat us. We did have access to the toilet. We got a piece of bread, maybe with a tiny amount of marmalade or something. We had no opportunity to wash ourselves, and we were covered in dried blood and stank. Most of the time, the beatings occurred in front of the other detainees to instil a sense of fear. Savo Cancarevic was present during most of these beatings." Is that a true and accurate statement of what happened over the next few days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now, you indicated that you were there three days, but you just testified that you were there and then they brought you back to the TO. Were they bringing you back and forth over the next few days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the following day, were you brought to the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell the Court what happened on the following day in relation to an interrogation that occurred.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day, I was interrogated by Mr. Milos Savic, an inspector in the then SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what condition were you in when you went there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had been beaten up. I could not control my own movements. I was not psychologically or physically ready to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to be questioned or interrogated at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me read this paragraph to you concerning that interview: "I was interrogated by Milos Savic, a police inspector. I knew him. I asked him at the end what was going on, what would happen to me. He said they need to take statements, and then they will release people. This never happened. He asked me general information about my family and my life. He also asked about weapons and how many tanks we had, and so on. I could not answer anything, as we had no weapons. He made me sign something. I did not read what it was, but he read something to me. All that was in this was personal details about my family history, marital status, my work and hobbies. I signed it, as I did not dare refuse. I was not beaten during this interrogation. Armed people would come into the room as this interrogation was going on. At the time I gave this interrogation, I had the same clothes, with all the bloodstains. I was bruised and deformed." Is that an accurate depiction of what happened on May 4th, during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were interrogated, did you remain in the SUP or did they bring you back across to the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remained at the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you held in the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They held me on the first floor of the police building, the room right next door to the room where I had been interrogated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the first floor," do you mean the ground floor or the first floor above the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first floor above the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P14A, photograph 53, please. Would you place that on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that building, first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that building of -- or what's depicted in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The building that I'm looking at is the backside of the police station in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does it show where -- or can you see in that photograph the window in relation to the room where you were being held for two days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That room right there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the top floor, last window on the left, was identified by the witness as the room where he was being held?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you know any of the other prisoners being held in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these persons civilians that were being held or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what ethnic group did they belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croat [As interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you spend your whole time in the SUP in that room, or did they hold you in any other room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not spend the entire room -- the entire time in that room. I was in other rooms at the SUP as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a matter of accuracy of the transcript. The question that my learned colleague posed was: Of what ethnic group did they belong? And what we heard the witness say, he answered: "He was a Croat." So the question was in plural, and the answer was: "He was a Croat." So maybe my learned colleague can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we want to clarify the record in relation to one of the answers. I had previously asked you whether the persons who were being held in that room with you at the SUP, or at the police station, were civilians or military persons, and you indicated that they were civilians. The next question was: "Of what ethnic group did those civilians belong?" And could you please answer that question: Of what ethnic group did those civilians who were being held with you belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, were you eventually returned to the Territorial Defence building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that on or about May 6th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that was probably the third time you had been to the Territorial Defence building. Now, on any of those occasions, any of those three occasions you had been to the Territorial Defence building, did you see any of the defendants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the building, or rather, at the Territorial Defence headquarters, no, but through the open door, through the open entrance door to the Territorial Defence, I saw, in front of the police station, Mr. Simo Zaric, but only in passing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you standing at the time when you saw the defendant Simo Zaric standing in front of the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of us were in the yard of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you doing in -- sorry. What's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I do believe that the answer of the witness was that he saw Simo Zaric only in passing, and the question next question of my colleague was: "When you saw the defendant Simo Zaric standing in front of the police station." So maybe the question was not following the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. It was a bit leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the yard of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a certain group of us, a group of prisoners who had been taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you being taken out for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just as they had taken us out before that, in order to maltreat us and hit us and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you saw Simo Zaric, what was he doing? Was he standing? Was he walking? Was he in a vehicle? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, I saw him in passing then. For a moment a man went by him and he stopped very briefly. I don't know whether he uttered a word or two, and then they parted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, also, let's look at that last time that you were at the Territorial Defence building. Were you visited on or about May 6th, 1992, by the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn that the Red Cross were going to be visiting that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the day I found out, the same day that they visited us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone tell you that they were going to be visiting you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That the International Red Cross would come and that we should pay attention to what we were going to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What condition were you and the other prisoners in when the Red Cross visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were beaten up, disfigured. Quite simply, we were incapable of any conversation or proper behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross visit on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do when they visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They made a list and they put questions. Most of the questions were identical: Did they beat you? How do you spend the day? How do you spend the night? Do you eat? Do you go to the toilet? Things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you answer them truthfully, that you had been beaten and you were barely receiving any food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why couldn't you tell the Red Cross that you had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell them for the following reason: When the persons from the International Red Cross walked into the room, the door remained open. The guards were about two or three metres away from us, and they could hear everything I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would have happened to you if you had told the truth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the Red Cross stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They stayed for as long as they needed to make this list. I don't know how much time it actually was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the TO, up to that date, from basically the TO and the police station, from the 2nd to the 6th, were you visited by anyone with any sort of medical background? Were you visited by any doctors, nurses, medical personnel of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Simic visit you and care for any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the next day, on May 7th. Were you transferred anywhere on May 7th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they move you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They moved us to the nearby village of Crkvina, to a warehouse facility of Agropromet, from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were moved to this warehouse facility owned by the Agropromet company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that warehouse owned by the Agropromet company, there was a total of 52 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all 52 from the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the others from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subsequently, a certain group of people came. Where they had been before that, I do not know, but what I know for sure is that they were from the municipality of Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown a group of photographs, 60, 61, 31, 32, and 63. 60 and 61 first, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at that photograph number 60. Could you tell us what that depicts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depicts the building where we were transferred from the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the warehouse in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you go to photograph 61, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that depicted in photograph 61?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Photograph 61 depicts the entrance door of the mentioned building where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you describe the inside of that building, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please describe it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for the interior of the building, there was no roof. There were just wooden planks. As soon as you'd walk in, on the other side there was a small office, perhaps one and a half metres by two metres, something like that. On the right-hand side, at the very end of the building -- I mean, at that moment when we walked in, there was a certain number of sacks. Now, whether this was seed or fertilizer for improving the quality of the land, I really don't know, but at any rate, there were some sacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of lighting did they have inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no lighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what material was the floor made out of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The floor was made of concrete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you sit on the concrete floor or did you sit on the sacks, or where did you sit when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we just got there, somebody was sitting on the sacks, but since there wasn't enough room for all, then the rest sat on the concrete floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now could the Witness be shown photographs 31, 62, and 63, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interior of the building where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would the door, the entry door that we just saw in the previous picture, be located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you place photograph 63 there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. This building, though, that we're seeing now has a roof, and the witness had said there was no roof. Could we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was taken by -- this photograph was taken by a Netherlands police several years later, I believe 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I presumed that, but I mean for the sake of clarity, the witness has said there was no roof. Now we see a photograph with a roof. It might be useful to have that on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was this roof that you see depicted in this photograph on that building at that time that you were held there in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my previous statement, I said that there was no ceiling, but actually, I meant that there was a roof. I was trying to say that there was no attic. When we say "ceiling," we mean attic. But there was a roof, and I said that there were wooden planks. I meant that there were wooden planks underneath the roof itself. I hope that I have now clarified what I meant when I said then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please -- that's number 63 that's there now? Thank you. Let's move to about 10.00 p.m. on that evening, May 7th, 1992. Did something happen at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 10.00 on that date, on the 7th of May, three men came. Of the three of them, one of them was called Lugar, one Crni, and the third man was called Pukovnik, Colonel. But I heard a couple of times that they called him Debeli, fat man, and sometimes they called him Pukovnik. And they were trying to enter the premises, but the door to the building was locked. The front of the building has three small windows in the upper part of the building. One of them climbed up to that small window. How, I don't know. But it's true that he shone the interior of the building from that small window. He broke the window and he shouted at all of us to get up and to line up, which is what we did. He wanted us to open the door. We couldn't open the door because it was locked. He chose three men and ordered us to break down the door, and they broke down the door. They carried out this order. They came through this door that had been broken, those three men, and then after that followed what happened next, the murders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before the murders, let me ask you a few questions. Where were the guards who were guarding the prisoners at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards who were guarding us were around the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they stop those three men from entering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take the three men, one at a time. You indicated that one of them went by the name of Debeli. Did Debeli have anything in his hands when he came in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Debeli came into the building with a hunting rifle, with a sawed-off barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the other two that entered with Debeli?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was called Slobodan Miljkovic, Lugar, and the other one I only know by his nickname, Crni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take Crni first. Did Crni have any weapons or was he holding anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Crni had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the third person, Lugar, did he have anything in his hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Lugar had a flashlight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when they entered, where were the prisoners at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they entered the building, we were lined up against the wall, on the front side of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to lining up, where were you sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were sitting, like I said, some people were sitting on sacks and some people were sitting where they chose to, on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us look at photograph 63, which is on the ELMO. Could you show us where were the sacks at that time that the prisoners were sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the witness identified the wall towards the far end of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did they walk in to the building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is the place where the sacks were?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where the sacks were, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On which the prisoners were sitting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is the doorway in this photograph? Approximately where is the doorway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the witness is pointing to an area to the right of the sacks that are in that picture, if you're facing the picture, just to the right of those sacks. It's just outside the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, they told you to line up, you and the prisoners, to line up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who told you to line up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Lugar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you lined up, show us on the photograph where you were lined up, with the pointer. Which wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that they were lined up at the wall where the grain or seed sacks are now in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did Lugar, Debeli, and Crni do after they came in? You're lined up against that wall which is under the windows. What did they do, or where did they go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They entered the building and stayed somewhere in the middle of that space.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Lugar -- let's start off with Lugar. Was he standing or sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lugar was sitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was sitting on a chair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he facing the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Crni and Debeli? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Crni and Debeli were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did Lugar do? Did he do something with a flashlight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Lugar pointed the flashlight at each prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what would happen when Lugar would point the flashlight at a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lugar pointed the light at each individual prisoner and then they would pick people, Crni, Lugar, or Pukovnik, and they would pick people to come up to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened to those persons that were chosen to come up to Lugar? Let's start off -- do you know who the first one was that was chosen or selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jozo Antunovic was there, from Gornji Hasici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please tell the Tribunal, or the Trial Chamber, what happened after Jozo Antunovic was selected and approached Lugar, Debeli, and Crni. Tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he came up to the two of them, they started to beat him immediately, to hit him, so that Jozan, that's what we called him, Jozan, he fell down at their feet. And as soon as he fell, he got up right away and started to run around this building. And he was behaving in a way that was not quite clear to me, because I knew Jozan. So he started to speak in an unintelligible way and it seemed to me as if he had been hit on the lower back of the skull, and he had lost his capacity to talk and everything else. And then immediately he went up to the place where the sacks were, and he fell there and remained there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he fell, did Lugar do anything to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Lugar took Pukovnik's rifle, put two bullets into the barrel. This was a hunting rifle. And he fired both bullets into Jozan. .

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to this man Jozo, or Jozan, after he was shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After those two bullets, they turned their attention to us. They left Jozan there. But after a few minutes, Jozan was showing some signs of life. He was making a kind of gurgling noise, and Lugar heard that and he took the rifle again and put a bullet inside and fired once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he strike Jozan when he fired this third bullet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say "did he strike," did he shoot him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after he shot him this third time, did Jozan, or Mr. Antunovic, show any signs of life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you, with that picture, show us where Jozan was when he was shot and killed, using the pointer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The sacks were here, and he was right in front of the sacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness is pointing middle to the rear of the -- it looks like the left wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were any other persons called out after Mr. Antunovic was shot and killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please go on and tell us what happened to the next man that got called.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next man was beaten up, and afterwards he fainted. He lost consciousness. But then when he came to again, they sent him down where the bags were, the sacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who decided that that second man should be beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who decided, but it's a fact that anybody who came to Lugar, Debeli, or Crni, was either beaten or killed. Nobody managed to get away without punishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second man, did this process begin with Lugar shining the flashlight on him too, just as he did with the first man, Mr. Antunovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Lugar shone the flashlight, he was told to come forward. Who beat him then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't be specific, but it was either Debeli or Crni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior to the beatings, or the shootings of Mr. Antunovic and this second gentleman, were they questioned? Were either of these persons questioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please explain your question? Are you thinking before this happened?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. No. Before -- let's go back to Crkvina. The light would be -- Lugar would shine a light on a prisoner, the prisoner would leave the line, approach Lugar, and at some point a decision was made whether to shoot him or beat the person. Prior to that decision to be made, whether to beat or shoot the person, did they question that person? Did they ask him any questions: How old are you? What's your name? Where do you live? Where were you born? Were you asked any questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of questions were asked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were asked their names, where are they from, where do they live, where do they work, do they have a wife, do they have children. Mostly they were just questions out of curiosity. They weren't provocative questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second man was spared. Were you called out? Did they shine the flashlight on you and did you have to step forward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Court what happened to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was called out. I don't remember exactly which one I was. Maybe I was the fourth or the fifth. I don't know exactly. But then when I stood in front of them, Debeli hit me with that same rifle, because before he took it from Mr. Lugar. So he hit me with the rifle on my head. I fell down immediately, and I crouched in order to protect myself from the following blows. I did receive a lot of blows and kicks in the area of my kidneys and my head. I lost my consciousness and I was left lying there. I don't know for how long. But the others told me that it wasn't longer than three or four minutes. Then I came to again and then they took me, and then I also went there to the place where the bags were, the sacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next man who was called out, do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Josip Orsolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they called out Josip Orsolic, they asked him for his name, where he was from, is he married. Josip said, "Yes, I am married. My wife is a Serb." And he probably thought that that would make it easier for him if he gave such an answer. And then Crni cursed his mother and said, "How could you have married a Serbian woman?" And he pointed a pistol to his temple. And he told him, "I will kill you now." And at that moment, Josip said, "Please don't kill me." And Crni, he didn't have any mercy, and he fired the pistol into Josip's temple, and he fell down immediately and he wasn't showing any signs of life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point to -- using that picture, could you please point to the area where Crni shot Josip in the head and killed him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would just like to say that all the murders were happening right here in this part, except for Josip Antunovic, who was the last person who was shot with the last bullet, and he was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The witness indicated that the murders occurred in front of the sacks that are there, and Josip's murder was across from the sacks, going away from the sacks, across towards the opposite wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the murder of Josip, that's two murders, how many people were killed in this first round of killings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nine people were killed. But I just wanted to add something to my previous answer. When I mentioned the places where the killings took place, I'm thinking about the first round of the killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's what we're talking about right now, the first round of killings. Now, the other seven men that were killed, did that follow the same process, where Lugar would first shine a light on that person, they would come out, step out in front of the line, approach Lugar, Crni, and Debeli, and some sort of decision would be made whether to murder them or beat them? Is that the process that continued to follow? I'm also assuming that after being questioned, a decision was made whether to murder them or beat them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to read a note from your statement as to the names of the persons that were killed. Paragraph 60: "I can name nine men who were killed during this round of questioning, from the opstina Bosanski Samac. Their names were Josip Orsolic, about 50 years old, from Domaljevac; Luka Gregurevic, about 35 to 38 years old, from Domaljevac; Jozo Antunovic, about 35 years old, from Gornji Hasici; Luka Blazanovic, about 35 years old, from Donji Hasici; Niko Brandic, about 30 to 32 years old, from Donji Hasici; Ilija Matic, about 45 years old, from Babina Greda, Croatia; Ivo Mijic, about 38 years old, from Grebnice; Ivan Agatic, about 25 years old, from Tursinovac; and a man from Bosanski Samac who was about 30 to 33 years old." Were those the persons that were murdered on that evening in the first round of the killings by Lugar, Crni, and Debeli?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that first group of nine people were murdered, what did Lugar do next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an order to move to the opposite wall, to line up along the wall, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the pointer, could you show us the wall that you had to line up after the first set of murders or the first set of killings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness has identified the wall which is opposite the seed bags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you lined up with the other prisoners at that wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were Lugar, Debeli, and Crni at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, Lugar switched places, but he was also sitting in the chair. Debeli and Crni stayed in the same place, in the middle of the room. That was where they were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you said Lugar switched places, do you mean he turned the chair around to face the new wall, or the opposite wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Lugar do with the flashlight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was doing the same thing that he was doing before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just tell the Court what he did next.
